questions.stem: Which knot makes a fixed loop that does not slip?
questions.explanation: The bowline makes a fixed loop that does not slip or tighten. A clove hitch is a quick temporary hold on a post, a sheepshank shortens a rope and an overhand knot is a simple stopper that is hard to untie once tight.

questions.stem: You must join a thick mooring line to a thin messenger line. Which knot is the right choice?
questions.explanation: The sheet bend joins ropes of different size, and the double sheet bend holds even better and jams less. A reef knot is the common tie for lines of the same size and is unreliable with unequal ropes. A figure of eight is a stopper and a sheepshank shortens one rope.

questions.stem: What is the main property of a rolling hitch?
options: It joins two ropes of equal size
It grips along a rope or spar and resists slipping in the direction of pull
It makes a loop in the middle of a rope
questions.explanation: The rolling hitch resists slipping along the rope or spar it is tied to, in the direction of pull, which is why it is used to attach a smaller line to a larger one and for stoppers. Joining equal ropes is the reef knot's job, loops come from a bowline and shortening from a sheepshank.

questions.stem: A knot is described as a quick, temporary hold on a post or rail that can jam under load. Which is it?
questions.explanation: The clove hitch is two half hitches that form a jamming hold, suited to quick, temporary securing on a post, spar or rail. A bowline is a fixed loop, a double sheet bend joins ropes, and the fisherman's bend fastens a hauling line to a ring.

questions.stem: What is the purpose of a figure of eight tied in the end of a rope?
options: To stop the end running out through a block or fairlead
To attach the rope to a hook
questions.explanation: The figure of eight is a stopper knot: it stops the rope unreeling through a block. A sheepshank shortens, a bend joins and a blackwall hitch holds a rope to a hook.

questions.stem: A mooring line is too long for the cleat and you do not want to cut it. Which knot shortens it, and what is a caution about it?
options: Sheepshank; the bights may be seized or toggled to the standing parts to make it dependable
Cat's paw; it holds in any condition
Bowline; it must be tied under load
questions.explanation: A sheepshank shortens a rope without cutting it. It holds only while there is a steady pull, so the bights can be seized or toggled to the standing parts to make it dependable. A reef knot is a tie, a cat's paw makes a loop for a tackle hook and a bowline makes a fixed loop.

questions.stem: Which pairing of knot and job is correct?
options: Cat's paw: temporary loop for hooking on a block of a tackle
Reef knot: joining ropes of very different thickness
Timber hitch: making a permanent fixed loop
questions.explanation: A cat's paw makes a temporary loop to hook on a block. A reef knot is for lines of the same size, a fisherman's bend secures a hauling line to a kedge ring or a bucket, and a timber hitch is a quick hold on a spar or plank rather than a permanent loop.

questions.stem: You are dragging a spar along the deck with a timber hitch. The pull is steady and must be directed. What should you add?
options: A second timber hitch next to the first
A reef knot in the standing part
Nothing: a timber hitch is secure by itself under continuous pull
questions.explanation: A timber hitch is a quick hold; for a continuous strain or where the pull must be directed, it is supplemented with a half hitch. A reef knot or a second timber hitch does not give the same result and the hitch alone is not recommended for continuous strain.

questions.stem: Which statement is correct about two half hitches and the fisherman's bend?
options: Two half hitches secure a rope end to a bollard or ring; the fisherman's bend secures a hauling line to a kedge ring
Two half hitches join two ropes; the fisherman's bend makes a loop
questions.explanation: Two half hitches are used for securing a rope end to a bollard or ring and for mooring. The fisherman's bend is also a hitch to a ring (it is also called the bucket hitch). Neither joins ropes, makes a loop or shortens a rope.

questions.stem: How many knots, bends and hitches (including whippings, seizings and stoppers) are on the knot list in the Bridge Watch Rating course standard TP 10936?
questions.explanation: The list in the course standard as summarised in our research has 25 items. If your instructor has a different edition, follow the current TP 10936.
